entries.title: How a jet engine pushes a plane forward
entries.answer: One kind of jet engine pulls air in and squeezes it through a row of spinning blades. Fuel burns in the crowded air and heats it. The hot gas expands so fast that it can turn another set of blades, called a turbine. The turbine keeps the front blades turning. Gas released at high speed from the rear can push the airplane forward. Many airliner engines also drive a big fan that moves air around the hottest part of the engine.
facts: Air, not just the burning fuel, carries much of the energy and push out of the back.

entries.title: How a subway carries people across a city
entries.answer: A subway runs trains frequently between stations where many people want to travel. Tunnels let the railway go below busy streets, but some sections may run outside or on bridges. Many subway trains have electric motors that draw power from a separate rail or overhead wires. Stations and switches create a network, so riding sometimes means changing trains. Signals and schedule plans help maintain space between trains, even when several run along the same track.
facts: The London Underground and New York City Subway are examples of city rail systems.

entries.title: How a train can float over its guideway
entries.answer: A maglev train uses magnets to lift and guide it instead of ordinary wheels doing all the work. Some designs carry magnets on the train that interact with electric coils along the track. These magnetic forces can keep a gap under the train while other coils push or pull it along. With less rubbing between train and guideway, there is less contact friction. The air still pushes against it, and the whole system needs a specially built route.
facts: Some maglev trains still use wheels at low speeds.

entries.title: How an electric car moves and recharges
entries.answer: An electric car stores energy in a large battery. An electric motor turns the wheels to make the car move. When the driver slows down, some cars can use the turning wheels to drive that same motor like a generator. That changes some of the car’s motion back into electrical energy the battery can store. The car still needs to be plugged in regularly because some of the energy is transferred to the air and other surroundings as warmth and cannot all be recovered.
facts: Regenerative braking cannot recover all the energy that the car used to get moving.

entries.title: How can a ferry carry cars across water?
entries.answer: A car ferry has a deck built to carry cars while the boat moves. Some car decks are open to the air. At the shore, a ramp joins the dock and the ferry. Workers guide vehicles onto the deck and leave room for them to get back out. A ferry can connect places separated by a bay or river. It turns the water into part of the route.
facts: Some ferries carry passengers on foot as well as people traveling with vehicles.

entries.title: How can two car wheels turn at different speeds on a bend?
entries.answer: When a car goes around a bend, the wheels on the outside follow a wider path than the wheels on the inside. They cover more ground during the same time. A part called a differential lets a powered pair of wheels turn at different speeds while both can receive power. Without that freedom, the tires would have to slide or scrub much more each time the car turned.
facts: The speed difference between the inside and outside wheels is easier to picture on a tight turn.

entries.title: How do airplane wings and tails steer?
entries.answer: An airplane can point its nose up or down, turn it left or right, or tip one wing lower than the other. Moving parts push on flowing air to help make these turns. A pair of parts near the wing tips, called ailerons, help tip the airplane. A small moving surface on the tail helps raise or lower the nose. The rudder on the upright part of the tail helps swing the nose from side to side.
facts: Tipping a wing, lifting the nose and swinging the nose are called roll, pitch and yaw.

entries.title: How do train wheels follow a curve in the tracks?
entries.answer: Many train wheels become a little narrower in diameter toward their outside edge. On a curve, a wheel and its partner can shift sideways on the rails. The outside wheel can then roll on a part with a slightly bigger diameter. It travels farther in one turn, helping the pair follow the bend. A raised lip on each wheel can also help keep it on the track.
facts: The raised edge of a train wheel is known as a flange.

entries.title: How does a bicycle chain carry your push to the back wheel?
entries.answer: When you press a bicycle pedal, you turn a ring with teeth near your feet. The teeth catch the links of the chain and pull it around. At the back of the bike, the chain catches the teeth of another wheel. Turning this wheel can turn the back tire against the ground. The chain carries motion between the pedals and the rear wheel even though they sit apart.
facts: A chain bends around a toothed wheel because its links can turn a little where they join.

entries.title: How does a jet airplane slow down on a runway?
entries.answer: A passenger jet may use several things to slow down on the runway. Brakes act on some wheels as they roll. Panels called spoilers can rise on the wings and reduce lift, so the wheels press harder on the ground and the brakes can work better. On some jets, the engines can also direct some of their flow forward to push against the plane’s motion.
facts: A wing’s spoilers can also add air resistance when they stand up in the flow.

entries.title: How does a small tug help move a big ship?
entries.answer: A cargo ship can travel far across the open sea, but moving it sideways near a dock can be hard. One or more tugboats can help by pushing against its side or pulling through a strong line. Each tug adds a push or pull in a chosen direction. That helps the crew guide the bigger ship through a crowded place or turn it at low speed.
facts: A tug that pushes against a ship often has thick bumpers along the part that touches it.

entries.title: How does regenerative braking save energy as a car slows?
entries.answer: Some electric and hybrid vehicles use their motor to help slow the wheels. The turning wheels drive the motor like a generator, which makes electricity from motion. The vehicle can store some of that electrical energy in its battery and use it later. Some energy still escapes as heat and other losses. Many vehicles also use brakes with rubbing pads when more stopping force is needed.
facts: Regenerative braking is the name for collecting some of a vehicle’s energy as it slows.

entries.title: How gliders fly without an engine
entries.answer: A glider has wings but no engine to keep it moving forward. After a launch or a tow, the glider normally loses height as it moves through still air. That sinking motion helps keep its speed so the wings can keep making lift. It can stay up much longer if the pilot finds air that is rising. Warm air rising from the ground or wind flowing up a hill can carry a glider higher.
facts: A glider’s long wings help it cover a lot of distance for the height it loses.

entries.title: How helicopters hover and turn
entries.answer: A helicopter’s main rotor spins long blades through the air. Each blade pushes air down and receives an upward push. The aircraft can hover when this upward force balances its weight. Changing the angle of the blades during each turn lets the pilot tip the main push and move in a chosen direction. Many helicopters also have a small tail rotor that keeps the body from turning the other way as the main rotor spins.
facts: Some helicopters use two main rotors turning in opposite directions instead of a tail rotor.

entries.title: How steam turned a locomotive’s wheels
entries.answer: A steam locomotive carries a boiler that heats water until it becomes steam. Pressure builds as the steam is kept inside. When admitted into a cylinder, the steam pushes a piston along the cylinder. Rods link that back-and-forth movement to turning wheels, a bit like your leg moves down on a bicycle pedal to turn it. The locomotive has to carry or stop for both fuel and water to keep that work going.
facts: The big rods beside the wheels are part of the machine that transmits the piston’s push.

entries.title: How submarines dive and rise
entries.answer: A submarine floats when water pushes upward as strongly as gravity pulls it downward. To dive, it lets seawater enter some tanks, replacing air. Its mass rises while its outer size stays about the same. It then sinks lower. To return to the surface, it can push water out of those tanks with air, becoming lighter again. When moving under water, a submarine can also use small movable fins to help control its depth.
facts: Air and water are used to adjust the submarine’s overall density.

entries.title: What happens when you squeeze a bicycle brake lever?
entries.answer: On many bicycles, squeezing a handlebar lever pulls a cable or pushes fluid through a tube. At the wheel, this makes two pads press against a moving surface. The surface might be the rim of the wheel or a metal disc fixed near its center. The rubbing slows the wheel and turns some of its energy into heat. Taking pressure off the lever lets the pads move away again.
facts: A disc brake grips a disc that turns with the wheel.

entries.title: What helps an airplane land without a hard slam?
entries.answer: Many airplanes land on wheels held by parts called landing gear. The gear carries the plane’s weight against the ground and lets the plane roll during takeoff and landing. Many designs have parts that compress or flex when the wheels touch down. They help soften the sudden push from the ground. Some airplanes fold their landing gear inside after takeoff so less air pushes against it in flight.
facts: Small planes can have gear that stays outside the whole time.

entries.title: Why airplanes change the shape of their wings
entries.answer: If you look out at a plane’s wing near landing, parts along the back may slide out or tilt down. These parts are called flaps. They change the size or shape of the wing so it can make more lift while moving more slowly. Flaps can also add drag, which helps a plane slow down. On flights that are cruising quickly, the flaps usually move back into the wing so the air can flow past more easily.
facts: Some wings also have movable parts on the front edge that help with slow flight.

entries.title: Why can a bicycle coast while its pedals stay still?
entries.answer: Many bicycles have a part that lets power move one way from the pedals to the back wheel. It catches when you pedal forward, so the chain can drive the wheel. When you stop pedaling and the wheel keeps rolling, the catching parts can slide past each other instead. The tire can keep turning while the chain and pedals pause. This is why you can coast downhill.
facts: Some bikes make a clicking sound when the back wheel turns faster than pedaling drives it.

entries.title: Why high-speed trains need special tracks
entries.answer: Fast passenger trains such as Japan’s Shinkansen use carefully built routes. Gentle curves help keep the sideways pull small at speed. Dedicated tracks can keep slower trains and road crossings out of the way. Each train still has to push through air, so a smooth shape helps limit drag. Timetables, signals and automatic train controls help keep enough space between trains. The result is rapid travel between cities with many people riding on one train.
facts: Japan’s first Shinkansen route began regular service in 1964.

entries.title: Why might a package travel by train and truck on the same trip?
entries.answer: A freight train can carry many loads between places linked by railroad tracks. A truck can reach roads and buildings well beyond those tracks. On some trips, people use both kinds of transport. A container can move onto a train for the long part of a trip and then onto a truck that takes it closer to its destination. The boxes inside that container may not need to be moved one at a time when the carrier changes.
facts: Freight trains can also carry materials like grain in railcars made for that load.
